key_insight: Intensity-modulated photoluminescence spectroscopy (IMPLS) can measure perovskite charge-carrier lifetime at a defined operating injection level, even in devices where conventional methods are obscured by capacitive and interfacial effects.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical frequency-domain diagnostic for optimizing perovskite films, transport layers, and solar-cell stacks under realistic illumination conditions.
method: Measure photoluminescence response under modulated excitation at operating conditions
Extract lifetime at a specific injection level from the frequency response
Use a transfer function to separate charge transfer from interface recombination in multilayer stacks
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that IMPLS matches steady-state PL lifetimes on thin films and reveals a third characteristic frequency in devices, enabling direct lifetime extraction where IMVS can fail.
watch_item: In perovskite/transport-layer stacks and full devices, the response becomes more complex, so interpreting the spectrum requires a dedicated transfer-function model rather than a direct single-frequency readout.
paper_title: Operando Charge Carrier Dynamics by Intensity-Modulated Photoluminescence: From Perovskite Thin Films to Solar Cells
